text:
kevin: Customer in DE on Private asked for direct SIEM TLS over TCP/6514 + HSM (PKCS#11). They also uploaded a container scan flagging openssl 1.1.1c in the appliance base image. Need plan and who owns what.

anya: Do we have a precedent for PKCS#11 HSM integration for Private? I recall a prototype but not production docs.

ben: We have a bridging adapter in prototypes that speaks to external HSM via PKCS#11. Not in the default delivered package. Rough effort: add PKCS#11 module + unit tests + packaging.

ops: Key constraints from customer: keys must never leave their HSM, must sign exported logs, and we must support mutual TLS to their SIEM gateway. No wide egress allowed.

security-oncall: Triage notes: 1) Confirm vulnerability scope: runtime vs build-time. 2) If openssl is used in a running binary (e.g., rsyslog with TLS), treat as high priority for patching. 3) Enable temporary hardened forwarding path to their SIEM through a gateway pod with mTLS and strict NetworkPolicy. 4) Capture full vuln report and keep artifacts.

deploy-bot: ticket SEC-4682 created for openssl remediation.

marco: I'll own the NetworkPolicy and pod gateway. Plan: create a dedicated namespace (siem-ingest). Deploy a tiny gateway container (haproxy/rsyslog) with mounted PKCS#11 module. NetworkPolicy will deny by default and permit only egress to the customer's gateway IPs and ports.

kevin: Example NetworkPolicy for the gateway namespace? Keep it minimal.

marco: paste below (replace IP):

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: siem-gw-egress
  namespace: siem-ingest
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      role: siem-gateway
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 198.51.100.10/32 # customer gateway
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 6514
```

anya: Also add egress for DNS to cluster DNS only, and no other external IPs. Use node-level firewall rules too if available.

ben: For the PKCS#11 integration: customer will give us a connector cert and a PKCS#11 SO path for their HSM gateway. We should mount it read-only and run the gateway as nonroot. Also ensure seccomp and no new capabilities.

security-oncall: Logging and audit: enable journald -> fluentd sidecar that writes to files signed locally with a transient envelope key. Then request the customer's HSM to sign the envelope key via Sign/Verify so they have non-repudiable proof. If HSM signing not possible, use customer-provided certificate chain and timestamping.

ops: For attestation, Compliance wants a short artifact (1 page) that states: component list, image digests, egress allowlist, KMS/HSM policy, audit retention, and signature verification steps. I can draft that.

kevin: Timeline suggestion: patch openssl in staging within 24-48 hours, deploy gateway + netpol in staging for SIEM test (48-72h), then canary + prod in next maintenance window. Who takes the openssl build?

man: @ben?

ben: I can do the openssl rebuild and image refresh. Will produce a minimal diff patch and push to SEC-4682. Need CI creds to push images to the private registry.

ops: I've scheduled a maintenance window Saturday 02:00 UTC. Will create CHG-8001 and add SRE.

security-oncall: Add monitoring rules: if no syslog connection to customer's gateway for 5m -> alert P0. If signature verification fails for exported bundles -> alert P1 and block further exports. Capture pcap during test and store under restricted bucket for 90 days.

anya: One more gotcha: our default container image builder caches base layers. Make sure the fix rebuilds base image and updates image digests in the manifest we ship. Also sign the final image manifest.

marco: Noted. I'll add image digest checks to the staging validation checklist.

ben: Starting rebuild now, will attach logs to SEC-4682.

kevin: Thanks. Please keep updates in SEC-4682. I'll handle customer coordination for certs and HSM access.
